resolutions.researcher_notes: The existing ref (attaqa.net / al-Taqa, 2023-09-17) was flagged DEAD_LINK by the harvest-time screen, but that was a false negative: the page is live (200) and its body literally states Agiba Petroleum ('عجيبة للبترول') brought the Framid gas field ('حقل فراميد') wells in the East White Desert area online in Sept 2023 at 25 mmscfd via a new 10-inch, 38km pipeline — the screen only failed because it was checking for the substring 'فرميد' (missing the alef) instead of the actual spelling 'فراميد'. Directly confirms Status=operating (production start reported, ongoing as of writing). Corroborated by masrawy.com (2023-09-17), which independently paraphrases the same facts (same 25 mmscfd, 10-inch/38km figures). Also found youm7.com (2023-09-17, verified OK, not included as a 3rd ref to avoid redundancy) reporting identical figures. All three trace to one origin — the Egyptian Ministry of Petroleum's Sept 17, 2023 Agiba Petroleum general-assembly statement (video-conference meeting chaired by the oil minister) — so per the 'same wire story, multiple outlets' rule these do not count as independent; tier capped at medium (1 strong effective source) rather than high. No contradiction found; SIS (state information service) coverage of the same event exists but the specific URL found is now 404/dead so it was not used.

No ref previously existed for Operator (blank). Same attaqa.net article names Agiba Petroleum Co ('عجيبة للبترول', chairman Tharwat El-Gendy) as the company that put the Framid field's gas wells into production — i.e. field/pipeline operator, matching the GEM Operator value exactly. Corroborated by youm7.com (اليوم السابع, one of Egypt's largest outlets), same date, same figures, also verified OK. Both, plus masrawy.com found in the same search, trace to the single Sept 17, 2023 Ministry of Petroleum / Agiba general-assembly statement, so treated as one effective origin per the shared-wire-story rule — tier medium, not high. Independent confirmation that Agiba (an EGPC/Eni-Lukoil JV, per company background sources) operates the East Obayed concession where Framid sits was also found (nsenergybusiness.com / worldoil.com 2018 Eni discovery coverage) but that predates the pipeline and was not cited as the primary ref since it doesn't name the pipeline itself. No contradicting operator name found anywhere.
